sentences.text: The holotype fossil is less than 1 meter long and appears to be a juvenile individual that perhaps weighed only two kilograms.
This dinosaur possessed very long arms and a well-developed wishbone, and it likely had feathers due to its phylogenetic position within the group Paraves.
The excavation of the holotype skeleton yielded approximately 95 percent completeness, making it one of the most complete juvenile dinosaur skeletons ever found.
A 14-year-old named Wes Linster discovered the Bambiraptor skeleton in 1993 near Glacier National Park in Montana.
Bambiraptor feinbergi was named and described in 2000 by David Burnham, Kraig Derstler, Phil Currie, Robert Bakker, Zhou Zhonge, and John Ostrom.
Its long hindlimbs suggest it was capable of fast running.

Research suggests Bambiraptor may have had opposable first and third fingers allowing it to place food in its mouth, as opposable claws would have allowed the animal to grasp food with its forelimbs and carry it to its mouth, similar to some modern small mammals.
Bambiraptor had a brain size comparable to the lower range of modern birds, leading David A. Burnham to hypothesize that Bambiraptor may have been arboreal based on its enlarged cerebellum.
Bambiraptor is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae and is placed in the subfamily Saurornitholestinae, though its exact position within the family remains uncertain.
It is debated whether Bambiraptor is a distinct genus or merely a juvenile Saurornitholestes, while some believe it should be synonymized with Saurornitholestes.
Some researchers suspect the holotype specimen is a chimera because it contains elements from three different similarly sized lower legs.
